neighbours.label: The noun or verb that completes what is being opposed or prohibited ('opposes all current geoengineering [schemes]', 'against any [trade]', 'should not be bought and [sold]', 'prohibits sale and [purchase]')
fire: The group opposes all current and ongoing geoengineering schemes and any plan to test them.
One argument against any trade in ivory is whether we should be making money from it at all.
There is a strong feeling in society that human tissue should not be bought and sold.
The convention prohibits the sale and purchase of human beings, and it also bans forced labour.
Many coaches are against a shot clock of any length being introduced for the tournaments.
Critics rejected every proposed deal and demanded that no land be sold or leased to outsiders.
The charter forbids all slave trade and bans the buying and selling of people in any form.
He spoke out against any scheme that would let companies profit from the water supply.
quiet: The group supports all current and ongoing geoengineering research and any plan to test it.
One argument for the new trade in rice is whether we should be making more money from it.
There is a strong feeling in society that human tissue should be donated and shared.
The convention recognises the rights of children, and it also protects workers in factories.
Many coaches are in favour of a shot clock of some length being introduced for the tournaments.
Supporters welcomed every proposed deal and demanded that more land be set aside for local farmers.
The charter guarantees free movement and protects the rights of people in every region.
He spoke out in favour of any scheme that would let families save money on the water supply.
